answer: An island mapping market buys nadir images of each jetty. Buyers escrow one payment per public job ID, defined by location and capture window. A verifier checks signed camera telemetry and required coverage; an atomic ledger marks the job paid before releasing escrow. Aliases claiming the same job cannot collect again, even with altered file hashes. To earn more, an operator must supply another funded job's valid imagery. This assumes trustworthy telemetry and verification; never award signup bonuses.
